title: Flute
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS flute (maker and model unstated on the page)
summary: A Boehm concert flute assembled from published data: hole positions, bore, head-joint taper, cork and mouth-hole from Boehm's 1871 treatise as recomputed and measured by Miller (1922), the embouchure riser of a measured Pearl PF-661 from UNSW, and the player's mouth pressure and jet length from a published experienced-flautist measurement (de la Cuadra et al. 2008). All sixteen holes are in the model, closed ones as hard-closed chimneys; the three notes use the published simple fingerings. Nothing was fitted to the Iowa recordings. The embouchure radiates from its solved window under the player's lip (Coltman's measured coverage), with no authored loss. With the jet-island phase fix and a lip-jet card whose band is placed by the published Strouhal number of maximum jet amplification, D4 and G4 now sound their first register natively, with the same pitch for two jet seeds. A5, which needs the second register, sounds an octave low. It is a hybrid description, not one real flute, and the lip-jet card is a published-parameter estimate, not a measured card.
physics_present: fs-couple flue_loop: a jet driven by a blowing-pressure gesture, with the lip geometry, jet length and the mouth contraction law, acting on a connected duct network (fs-couple network performance, one jet drives the whole graph)

16 tone-hole branches as plane-wave chimney sections on ideal junctions, open or closed per fingering, with the published head-joint taper as stacked cylinders, the cork cavity and the embouchure riser
fractional-delay propagation and gas-derived viscothermal loss on every section of the network (moist air at the published measurement state)

radiation reaction and observation from the apertures themselves, so the graded sound is radiated pressure at a physical receiver rather than internal pressure: a compact baffled-piston load on every open hole and the open end, with every open aperture and the embouchure summed at the receiver (the computed mutual operator could not be used, see below)

a jet source whose amplification band is a magnitude and whose phase is the convective delay alone (island fix 1718d79fb), driven by a published-parameter lip-jet card (theta/b 1.75, convection ratio 0.4; X-Est, not a measured card): the first register speaks at the played Strouhal numbers

the embouchure's own radiation under the player's lip, with no authored loss (bead frankensim-5kfrn): the hole is the riser (the riser's area, Boehm's 10:12 across to along) through the head's outer cylinder at a + 5 mm, the lip plate's proxy, under a rigid lip on the player's side that leaves Coltman's open strip against the hole's far edge (6 mm at C4 to 3.5 mm at G6, via Fletcher 1975; D4 5.84, G4 5.44, A5 4.31 mm), with the player's face as a rigid half-plane through the bore's axis 1.8 mm behind the lip's edge (Fletcher 1975 p.235's dead interval, inside his 1 to 2 mm), solved in the window's exterior over the whole arc. The one-sided lip and the face together render D4, G4 and A5 10.8, 15.0 and 21.3 cents flat of the centred lip in free space, within 0.33 cent of the prediction on the solved loads written before the renders (12 of 12 predictions within 5 cents, the face at 1, 1.8 and 2 mm); the face leaves the radiation resistance the bare cylinder's. The numbers that follow compare the centred lip with the authored loss. fs-bem's wall window solves it as a staircase ladder at 16, 32 and 64 axial cells (observed order 0.95 to 1.35; the lip's knife edge converges at first order, checked against Lamb's slit grating to 0.35 %), and the Junger-Feit series on the solved outer face radiates it. Against the authored 0.02 loss, D4, G4 and A5 sound 12.0, 9.9 and 29.3 cents lower and their fundamentals 12.7, 14.9 and 20.6 dB stronger; the share above 2.8 kHz falls from 71 to 12 % on G4 and from 73 to 5 % on A5 but only from 19 to 18 % on D4, whose level sits in H7 and H9 below 2.8 kHz. The piston bracket agrees within 0.1 cent; Dickens 2007's 25 % coverage (7.41 mm open) gives -4.6, +2.6 and -3.8 cents

the bore gas of a played flute, from Coltman's measurement on a flute (Physics Today 21(11), 1968, p.27; ledger coltman-1968-flute-bore-gas): one mean state of 26.15 C (the mean of his 26.5 and 25.8 C), saturated, CO2 2.5 percent dry and O2 18.5 percent dry paired from the shared breath pack's bracket, used by the bore, the holes, the window and the receiver alike. Against the earlier UNSW measurement state (25 C, 58 percent, no breath CO2) it lowers every passive mode by 3.2 cents (2.0 to 4.4 over his two end temperatures). A test holds the engine's CO2-only shift to his printed 'about 12 cents' within 2 cents. Rendered on one binary (463b75503) the native f0 falls 3.0, 3.0 and 3.2 cents on D4, G4 and A5 and nothing else moves (harmonic levels within 0.4 dB, share above 2.8 kHz within 0.2 points). Against the Iowa notes the f0 error goes -5.5 to -8.5 cents on D4 (worse) and +18.8 to +15.8 on G4 (better), and no graded measure changes verdict (2 of 15 and 4 of 15 inside the ruler, before and after); A5 stays in the first register and is still refused. The gas is the measured state of a played flute, kept whatever the direction of the pitch change
physics_missing: a measured lip jet: the opt-in published jet transfer (Price, Johnston and McKinnon 2015, with a measured phase velocity) was NOT run on this flute, because its control, the tin-whistle ladder at the paper's flows, did not self-sustain (all four renders silent, gate 2 of pexfp.320). The lip jet is classed a short channel (de la Cuadra 2005 Sec. 3.1, decided before any flute ramp), and the playing-condition jet gain is UNKNOWN (u-jet-playing-gain)
a tone-hole model beyond a plane-wave chimney on an ideal junction: no matching-volume or end-correction treatment of the junction, no pad cups, no undercut

a broadband, mutually coupled radiation model: the computed operator admits at most eight openings and is fitted to the mechanics Nyquist, where its baffled-piston quadrature fails at the clock this flute needs; the compact load holds only for ka up to 0.5 and so limits the receiver band to about 2.8 kHz, far below the flute's harmonic content; the holes also sit on a cylinder in the real flute but are placed in a flat baffle plane here

the player's real face, the lip's thickness and the lip plate's shape: the face is a rigid half-plane through the bore's axis and the lip a rigid cover lying on the outer cylinder, the lip plate's proxy. With them the head's end correction at f0 is 32.3 to 37.8 mm (bore-referenced, from the prediction mirror on the solved loads), against 43 to 60 mm that Vauthrin 2015 measured with a player, so the face's angle, shape and extent, the lip's thickness and the lip plate are still worth tens of cents flat. The face's setback is Fletcher's 1.8 mm inside his 1 to 2 mm (a 2.5 to 4.9 cent span), and how the coverage changes with dynamic is unknown (u-lip-coverage, u-lip-side, u-player-face, u-lip-plate)

frequency-dependent loss above 3 kHz, and any loss in the tone-hole chimneys and the riser: the viscothermal cell needs rate of about fifty times its band edge, so loss is selected only on bore sections of 17 mm or more and only to 3 kHz
the true head-joint taper profile (only the two published endpoints are known; it is a stack of cylinders on a straight line between them) and a convergence ladder on that stacking

a flutist's lip jet: the jet card in use is an inline estimate for a lip jet built from published parameters, not a measured card, the jet displacement gain is the demonstrator value, the labium offset is another player's measured reference jet (Onogi 2021, one player, +0.29 +- 0.30 mm), the jet angle is already inside that offset, and the onset ramp is authored

a temperature, oxygen and humidity profile along the bore: the bore gas is one mean state from Coltman 1968, not a profile. His two end temperatures alone move the pitch by 1.2 cents either way, the O2 pairing by 0 to +2.3 cents and the saturation by 0 to -4.8 cents (unknowns u-bore-gas-profile and u-bore-gas-composition)
a same-specimen impedance pair, so the passive chain is checked only against the pooled UNSW statements, not against a measured impedance of this flute
wall and pad vibration, fork fingerings (F sharp, B flat), vibrato, and the register-hole and trill-hole notes

the overblown register transition: not reproduced. Natively the first register persists up to the strongest jet tried, at every step count of the gate's rate ladder, and the level at that strongest jet still changes with the step count, so that regime is not converged. The published octave jump (de la Cuadra 2008) is therefore not claimed, and the second-register note (A5) sounds the first register of its fingering, an octave low. An earlier Python mirror showed isolated higher-register points that moved with the sample rate; the native runs do not, so those were a mirror artifact. A card-by-geometry test (the same pressure sweep or measured flows, with the jet card swapped on a fixed geometry) shows that whether the registers stage follows the jet card, not the geometry: the lip-jet card does not stage on the flute geometry nor on the tin-whistle geometry, while the windway-jet card stages the whistle at its measured flows. So the missing overblow of the flute points at its lip-jet card, an estimate, and not at its bore or holes. The windway-jet card is no substitute: on the flute geometry it sounds high partials of the pipe at the playing pressure

a spectrum like a real flute: one player's measured labium offset (+0.29 mm) makes the cut asymmetric, but with the demonstrator gain the even harmonics stay faint: H2 is 51 (D4) and 58 (G4) dB below H1, against -0.5 and +1.3 dB in the Iowa recordings, and across that player's -0.01 to +0.59 mm H2/H1 spans -80 to -45 dB (D4) and -88 to -52 dB (G4) with no pitch change. The jet swings 117 (D4) and 204 (G4) cut half-widths RMS at the labium (the island's own eta_rms/b; 53 and 92 mm against cut-ups of 8 and 7.1 mm), so the labium switches as a relay, the cut is a square wave and the odd harmonics stay strong (D4 H7 and H9 2.6 and 7.8 dB below H1, against 18.9 and 25.7 dB in the recording); the radiation band is also capped by the compact load. The opt-in forced Bickley jet (`jet_response forced-bickley 0.1 90`) still swings 17 and 23 half-widths and sounds both notes an octave high (594 and 808 Hz, pexfp.135.1), so it is not selected. A breakup amplitude bound (de la Cuadra 2005, Eq. 2.16 with its cube root) would not help: at the cards' jet Strouhal numbers (0.012 to 0.014) it sits 17 to 19 cut half-widths out, where the cut is already fully switched. The acoustic velocity in the window is plausible (4.8 % of the jet speed RMS at D4); what is missing is the jet's transfer from acoustic velocity to displacement at the flute's Reynolds number, not a saturation. Measured 2026-10-29 on origin 7cd604146, whose renders of these cards are bit-identical to the published audio

a pitch claim: the passive first octave stretches. Against Miller's note-independent closed-end correction (51.5 mm, Miller 1922 pp.34-36) this network's passive first mode runs from -10 cents at C4 to +96 cents at C5 against equal temperament at A=440 in the card gas, a C4 to C5 interval stretched by 106 cents, and against the first impedance minima of a measured Pearl PF-661 (UNSW pages, digitised at 10 Hz per pixel) its correction spread over C4 to C5 is 22.9 mm against 4.6 +- 6.6 mm (rejected at 2.8 sigma), with a gap of +1 to +40 cents from C4 to F4 and +72 to +107 cents from G4 to C5 (+55 to +82 with the Pearl's own hole positions and diameters, Wolfe and Smith 2003 Table I). Excluded as the cause: hole positions (0.000 mm from Miller), diameters, the open sets (identical to the specimen's for C4 to G#4), the cited tone-hole terms (matching volume, inner and series length, cylinder flange: net +3 to +7 cents), the lattice cutoff (2174 against 2050 +- 400 Hz), the cross-fingering response (-13.9 against -15 +- 5 cents), a 2.5 mm riser (spread 19.4 mm), the window length and the cork distance. An independent transfer-matrix chain built from Miller's geometry (Keefe loss and holes, conical head, embouchure chimney) stretches as much (27.4 mm), so a head-joint or embouchure term is missing and unidentified, not a defect in how the network is built (the network's own solver was not driven passively: that rests on three native renders sitting 12 to 20 cents below the passive minima, jet pull and loss); the jet loading and this term together decide the pitch, not a verified model

native verification beyond two notes: the jet-island fix is verified natively on D4 and G4 at one mechanics clock and two jet seeds, and on a plain pipe at three mechanics clocks (tests/flue_jet_phase.rs: same lock, level within a few percent); the flute itself has not been rendered at more than one clock, because its viscothermal loss cells fix the clock

a jet island that reproduces the overblowing ladder of the edge-tone gates: the gates were moved from the interim slot-jet card, which is outside its own validity band at every row, to the lip-jet card (gate change 5d77b0a49). Natively the cut-up direction gate (cut-ups taken from the published first-register window, a longer cut-up locks the same or a lower register) and the labium-duty gate hold. The overblowing-ladder gate is RED: no pressure of the sweep locks the second register and the first register persists to the strongest jet, the same finding as the overblown-register item above. The linear loop analysis agrees with the native rows at low pressure (the lowest rows are linearly stable, the next are barely unstable and oscillate only at tiny amplitude). At the top of the sweep it gives the second register the larger linear margin, but both registers are far above threshold and the first register's saturated cycle persists, with a cold start as well as with a ramp. Diagnosis from time-domain mirror runs and the native diagnostics: the island's authored displacement gain, set from the inviscid linear-stability maximum, swings the jet by many jet half-widths at the labium, so the labium switches like a hard relay and the established first-register cycle fixes the switching times. Compressing the deflection does not change that and an amplitude-dependent labium loss does not either; lowering the gain does move the register boundary, so the missing physics is a measured, viscous-limited jet amplification (profile broadening along the cut-up). It needs a cited amplification value that has not been obtained, so the gain is left unchanged. The interim-card gates were green before the phase fix and red after it, and that old green is not evidence that the original island was right
